## 4. Decisions

| Id | Question | Decision |
|----|----------|----------|
| D1 | Where the format lives | A new module `paigasus-gateway-core::responses` (`classify`, `assembly`, `stream`, `body`), with its own `Protocol` implementation. It shares only the generic parts: `json`, `sse`, `report`, `interceptor`, `body`, `turn`. `ChoiceAssembly` does not change. |
| D2 | New core types | `Format::OpenAiResponses`. `HoldKey::Response` (one hold per response, D10). New `ToolCallKind` variants: `Computer`, `LocalShell`, `Shell`, `ApplyPatch`, `ToolSearch`, `McpApprovalRequest`. `function_call` uses `Function`, `custom_tool_call` uses `Custom`. `ToolCall` gets `namespace: Option<String>`. |
| D3 | Server-side state | **Stateless only.** With interception enabled (the global `[tool_interception] enabled`, that is `AppState.tool_interception` is `Some`, known before admission), a request is refused with 400 `responses-stateful-not-supported` when it has a non-null `previous_response_id`, `conversation` or `prompt`, or an `item_reference` input item. |
| D4 | Background mode | `background: true` is refused with the same 400, whether interception is enabled or not. The gateway has no route for `GET /v1/responses/{id}`, so a background result cannot be fetched through it. |
| D5 | `store` | The request body is forwarded unchanged. The gateway does not set `store: false`. D3 already stops every later turn from reading the stored output. A rewrite of `store` would be the first request rewrite (749 non-goal). Operator note: with `store` true, OpenAI keeps the output, including a blocked call, for its retention period (§ 9). |
| D6 | Service shape | One generic handler pipeline with an endpoint descriptor per route (§ 8). `/v1/chat/completions` moves to it with no change in behaviour. The descriptor is for OpenAI-shaped routes. SMA-750 decides whether it extends it. |
| D7 | Upstream | `OpenAiClient` gets one method that takes a closed `UpstreamRoute` enum (`ChatCompletions`, `Responses`), never a free path. `Responses` forwards to `{base_url}/v1/responses` with the same headers, timeouts and cancellation as chat. |
| D8 | Route switch | A new `[responses] enabled` config key, default `false`. When it is `false`, `/v1/responses` returns 404. Rollback is this key, with no deploy. |
| D9 | Streaming switch | Streaming obeys the existing `stream_enabled`. No new capability is advertised (749 D28). |
| D10 | The hold | **One hold per response.** It opens at the first client-run item's `added` frame and completes at the terminal event. The decider gets every client-run call of the response in one `decide` call, as it gets every call of choice 0 in chat. A truncation (§ 6.4, R15) blocks every call of the hold with `Truncated`. |
| D11 | Output framing | Re-framed as in 749 D3, with an `event: <data.type>` line before each `data:` line. `unframed()` uses the same form. `[DONE]` has no `event:` line. |
| D12 | Rewrite | A blocked item becomes a `message` item at the same `output_index`, frame by frame (§ 6.5). No other index changes. |
| D13 | Abort frame | A new constant for this format: `"\n\nevent: error\ndata: {\"type\":\"error\",\"code\":\"upstream-error\",\"message\":\"upstream stream error\",\"param\":null}\n\n"`. The leading blank line ends a partly sent record, as in `TERMINAL_SSE_ERROR`. |
| D14 | Billing | A Responses usage reader (§ 8.2) with no 64 KiB record limit. 749 D24 applies: a rewrite does not change the charge. |
| D15 | Size limits | Per-format limits. For Responses: `max_record_bytes` 16 MiB, `max_held_bytes` 32 MiB, and a separate `[responses] max_request_bytes` of 16 MiB. These are first values. M7 checks them, and the plan records the measured sizes. Measured: `response.created` at most 60,507 bytes and `response.completed` at most 60,976 bytes, with 50 KB of `instructions` and 30 tools (M7, 2026-11-14). |
| D16 | Strict JSON | Per-format data subtrees and classifier keys (§ 7.1). The chat and Anthropic lists do not change (AC 8). |
| D17 | Request side | `parse_request(Format::OpenAiResponses, …)` builds `TurnFacts` (§ 7.2). |
| D18 | Client-run built-in items | Enforced like function calls (§ 6.2). They are held, decided and rewritten. |

### Reasons

- **D1.** Responses streams are item-based: each event has an `output_index` and an `item_id`, and
  `*.done` events repeat the full value. Chat Completions streams index-delta fragments. A shared
  assembly would put Responses cases into the code path that SMA-757 proved.
- **D3.** The gateway cannot see a turn that OpenAI stores. A decision then has no `prior_calls` or
  `tool_results`, and SMA-753 sequence rules fail open. A blocked call also stays in OpenAI's
  stored output, which the client never saw (M1). A `prompt` template can add tools that the
  gateway cannot see. With interception off, the gateway is a plain proxy, and these fields do no
  harm through it.
- **D8.** Billing and availability depend on shapes that are first measured in this change (M2,
  M7). An operator must be able to turn the route off without a deploy.
- **D10.** SMA-752 and SMA-753 policies that limit the calls per turn need every call of the turn
  in one decision. Chat gives them that per choice. A hold per item would give them one call at a
  time. The cost: frames after the first client-run item wait until the terminal event. Chat has
  the same cost until `finish_reason`.
- **D12.** A replacement at the same index keeps every later `output_index` valid. It needs no
  renumbering, which is the main cost of the chat rewrite.
- **D14, D15.** R-g. A lifecycle event over 64 KiB would charge only the estimate. A lifecycle
  event over 1 MiB would fail the stream, and every SDK raises without `response.created` or a
  terminal event. D3 also makes a client resend the whole conversation on every turn.
- **D18.** A shell command, a file patch or a mouse action has at least the risk of a function
  call. A report of "unenforceable" would let a client run an action that was never decided.

## 5. Types
-----
### 6.5 Rewrite

Only frames that contain a blocked item are re-serialized. A blocked item's frames are rewritten
one by one, so the rule works for a blocked hold, a truncated item, a hold limit and a stream that
fails while the item assembles (`Mode::Failed`):

- The item's `added` frame becomes three events: `response.output_item.added` with the message
  item, `response.content_part.added` with an empty `output_text` part, and
  `response.output_text.delta` with the notice (§ 6.6).
- Every middle frame of the item is dropped.
- The item's `done` frame becomes `response.output_item.done` with the completed message. When the
  item has no `done` frame, this event is synthesized before the next frame of the stream (the
  terminal event, `[DONE]`, EOF or the D13 frame), as chat's `closing()` does.
- In the terminal event, the item at a blocked index is always replaced with the completed message.
  This replacement is exempt from R10.

The exact JSON, with `<i>` the blocked `output_index`, `<n>` the notice, and `<s>` the
`sequence_number` of the replaced frame (the key is left out when R7 says none):

```json
{"type":"response.output_item.added","output_index":<i>,"sequence_number":<s>,
 "item":{"type":"message","id":"msg_paigasus_<i>","role":"assistant","status":"in_progress","content":[]}}
{"type":"response.content_part.added","item_id":"msg_paigasus_<i>","output_index":<i>,"content_index":0,"sequence_number":<s>,
 "part":{"type":"output_text","text":"","annotations":[],"logprobs":[]}}
{"type":"response.output_text.delta","item_id":"msg_paigasus_<i>","output_index":<i>,"content_index":0,"sequence_number":<s>,
 "delta":"<n>","logprobs":[]}
{"type":"response.output_item.done","output_index":<i>,"sequence_number":<s>,
 "item":{"type":"message","id":"msg_paigasus_<i>","role":"assistant","status":"completed",
         "content":[{"type":"output_text","text":"<n>","annotations":[],"logprobs":[]}]}}
```

The three events from one `added` frame repeat its `sequence_number`. The emitted numbers then do
not strictly increase. No SDK of § 3.2 reads `sequence_number` on a `create` stream (spec author's
call; the Python conformance test of § 10.2 confirms it for openai-python).

No other field of the terminal event changes: `status`, `usage`, `incomplete_details` and `error`
stay as the upstream sent them. If M2 shows a wire `output_text` field, the builder adds the
notice to it and records this here. The Responses API has no `finish_reason`, so nothing else is
rewritten.

**Non-stream.** The same replacement in the body's `output[]` (the completed message). 749 § 4.4
applies otherwise: one re-serialization, and the original bytes when nothing is blocked. A
client-run item with a `status` other than `"completed"` is blocked with code `Truncated` and
replaced, as in the stream (R15; preflight ruling F7).

### 6.6 Notice, names and report

749 § 4.5 and § 4.6 apply. The notice is `[paigasus] tool call "<name>" was blocked (<code>).`.
`<name>` is `ToolCall.name`, prefixed with `<namespace>.` when a namespace is present, then
sanitized. In a report, `choice` is `0` and `position` is the `output_index`.

## 7. Request side and strict JSON

### 7.1 Strict JSON per format

- The Responses data subtrees are: `tools[]` (whole entries), `text`, `metadata`, `instructions`,
  `prompt`, `reasoning`, and `input` (request); `response.tools`, `response.text`,
  `response.metadata`, `response.instructions`, `response.prompt` and `response.reasoning`
  (lifecycle events and the non-stream body). Below a data subtree, the `parse_value_strict` rules
  apply.
- `check_numbers` runs on the envelope and on each client-run item only, not on data subtrees.
- The Responses classifier keys (`type`, `output_index`, `item_id`, `call_id`, `item`, `output`,
  `arguments`, `input`, `name`, `namespace`, `id`, `delta`, `response`, `error`) are a per-format
  list. The chat and Anthropic lists do not change.

## 8. Service

### 8.1 The generic pipeline

An endpoint descriptor per OpenAI-shaped route:

```rust

    route: UpstreamRoute,          // D7
    format: Format,
    parse: fn(&[u8], bool /* interception */) -> Result<RequestFacts, ApiError>, // DTO, D3, D4
    estimate: fn(&RequestFacts, usize) -> u64,
```

The flow is the current chat flow (auth, body limit, parse, stream switch, `Limits::admit`,

updated.

### 8.2 Usage and the charge

- **Stream.** A Responses scanner reads a copy of the upstream bytes, as `UsageScanner` does
  (1 token per data record). For `response.completed`, `response.incomplete` and `response.failed`
  records, it reads `response.usage.total_tokens` with a streaming key scan that has no record size
  limit and holds no more than the scan state. The last value wins. Other records over 64 KiB are

  from `output[].content[].text`, `output[].arguments` and `output[].input`, by the chat rule

  item: `content` text (string or `input_text` parts), `arguments`, `input` and `output`.
- Tests: a terminal event over 64 KiB and one over 1 MiB are charged their reported usage, with
  interception on and off.

### Reasons

- **D1.** Responses streams are item-based: each event has an `output_index` and an `item_id`, and
  `*.done` events repeat the full value. Chat Completions streams index-delta fragments. A shared
  assembly would put Responses cases into the code path that SMA-757 proved.
- **D3.** The gateway cannot see a turn that OpenAI stores. A decision then has no `prior_calls` or
  `tool_results`, and SMA-753 sequence rules fail open. A blocked call also stays in OpenAI's
  stored output, which the client never saw (M1). A `prompt` template can add tools that the
  gateway cannot see. With interception off, the gateway is a plain proxy, and these fields do no
  harm through it.
- **D8.** Billing and availability depend on shapes that are first measured in this change (M2,
  M7). An operator must be able to turn the route off without a deploy.
- **D10.** SMA-752 and SMA-753 policies that limit the calls per turn need every call of the turn
  in one decision. Chat gives them that per choice. A hold per item would give them one call at a
  time. The cost: frames after the first client-run item wait until the terminal event. Chat has
  the same cost until `finish_reason`.
- **D12.** A replacement at the same index keeps every later `output_index` valid. It needs no
  renumbering, which is the main cost of the chat rewrite.
- **D14, D15.** R-g. A lifecycle event over 64 KiB would charge only the estimate. A lifecycle
  event over 1 MiB would fail the stream, and every SDK raises without `response.created` or a
  terminal event. D3 also makes a client resend the whole conversation on every turn.
- **D18.** A shell command, a file patch or a mouse action has at least the risk of a function
  call. A report of "unenforceable" would let a client run an action that was never decided.

## 5. Types
-----
### 6.5 Rewrite

Only frames that contain a blocked item are re-serialized. A blocked item's frames are rewritten
one by one, so the rule works for a blocked hold, a truncated item, a hold limit and a stream that
fails while the item assembles (`Mode::Failed`):

- The item's `added` frame becomes three events: `response.output_item.added` with the message
  item, `response.content_part.added` with an empty `output_text` part, and
  `response.output_text.delta` with the notice (§ 6.6).
- Every middle frame of the item is dropped.
- The item's `done` frame becomes `response.output_item.done` with the completed message. When the
  item has no `done` frame, this event is synthesized before the next frame of the stream (the
  terminal event, `[DONE]`, EOF or the D13 frame), as chat's `closing()` does.
- In the terminal event, the item at a blocked index is always replaced with the completed message.
  This replacement is exempt from R10.

The exact JSON, with `<i>` the blocked `output_index`, `<n>` the notice, and `<s>` the
`sequence_number` of the replaced frame (the key is left out when R7 says none):

```json
{"type":"response.output_item.added","output_index":<i>,"sequence_number":<s>,
 "item":{"type":"message","id":"msg_paigasus_<i>","role":"assistant","status":"in_progress","content":[]}}
{"type":"response.content_part.added","item_id":"msg_paigasus_<i>","output_index":<i>,"content_index":0,"sequence_number":<s>,
 "part":{"type":"output_text","text":"","annotations":[],"logprobs":[]}}
{"type":"response.output_text.delta","item_id":"msg_paigasus_<i>","output_index":<i>,"content_index":0,"sequence_number":<s>,
 "delta":"<n>","logprobs":[]}
{"type":"response.output_item.done","output_index":<i>,"sequence_number":<s>,
 "item":{"type":"message","id":"msg_paigasus_<i>","role":"assistant","status":"completed",
         "content":[{"type":"output_text","text":"<n>","annotations":[],"logprobs":[]}]}}
```

The three events from one `added` frame repeat its `sequence_number`. The emitted numbers then do
not strictly increase. No SDK of § 3.2 reads `sequence_number` on a `create` stream (spec author's
call; the Python conformance test of § 10.2 confirms it for openai-python).

No other field of the terminal event changes: `status`, `usage`, `incomplete_details` and `error`
stay as the upstream sent them. If M2 shows a wire `output_text` field, the builder adds the
notice to it and records this here. The Responses API has no `finish_reason`, so nothing else is
rewritten.

**Non-stream.** The same replacement in the body's `output[]` (the completed message). 749 § 4.4
applies otherwise: one re-serialization, and the original bytes when nothing is blocked. A
client-run item with a `status` other than `"completed"` is blocked with code `Truncated` and
replaced, as in the stream (R15; preflight ruling F7).

### 6.6 Notice, names and report

749 § 4.5 and § 4.6 apply. The notice is `[paigasus] tool call "<name>" was blocked (<code>).`.
`<name>` is `ToolCall.name`, prefixed with `<namespace>.` when a namespace is present, then
sanitized. In a report, `choice` is `0` and `position` is the `output_index`.

  R14). Measured: `computer_call` `actions` absent at `added`; `apply_patch_call`
  `operation.diff` `""` at `added`; `shell_call` `action.max_output_length` `null` at `added`.
- A3. R15 takes precedence over R11: a `done` with `status: "incomplete"` has partial JSON
  arguments in 9 of 9 cut calls. It is a truncation (block, `Truncated`), not `Malformed`.
- A4. Two event types that the openai-python 3.48.0 union does not have:
  `response.apply_patch_call_operation_diff.delta` and `.done`. They are known types now, mapped
  to `apply_patch_call`, with the diff rule in R14.
- A5. The openai-python `ResponseStream` model no longer counts `output_item.added` items as
  calls (§ 10.1). Under A2, an `added` item is a partial view by design.
----
## Review Focus

1. **A hostile `type` string in pass-through mode.** After `on_failure = allow` switches a stream to pass-through, `unframed()` writes `event: <data.type>` without classification. A `type` that holds `\n` (as a JSON escape) or a long string must not inject an SSE line. Expected: an `event:` line only when the type matches `^[a-z0-9_.]{1,64}$`; otherwise no `event:` line. Task 6 pins it.
2. **Explicit `null` in the D3 and D4 fields.** SDKs and frameworks can send `"previous_response_id": null`, `"conversation": null`, `"prompt": null` or `"background": false`. Expected: these pass. Only a non-null value (or `background: true`, or an `item_reference` item) is refused. Task 14 pins it.
3. **A non-stream body with a client-run item that is not `completed`** (for example `max_output_tokens` cut a function call, `status: "incomplete"`). The stream path calls this a truncation. Expected on the body path: fail closed, `Malformed("item_not_completed")`, so `block` answers 502 `tool-interception-malformed-response` and `allow` forwards the body unchanged. Task 5 pins it.
4. **A Responses stream with no client-run item but with provider-run items and text.** No hold opens. Expected: every payload is forwarded unchanged (re-framed with its `event:` line), one `: paigasus-decision` comment with `"decision":"unenforceable"` per provider-run item, and no decider call. Task 9 pins it in `allow_all_is_payload_identical_for_every_conforming_fixture`.
5. **A terminal event over the record limit with interception on.** A terminal event over 16 MiB is a stream failure (D8). Expected: the client gets the D13 path or the `(malformed)` rewrite as 749 § 6 says, and the charge is still the reported `response.usage.total_tokens`, because the usage scanner has no record limit. Task 13 pins the scanner half and Task 14 the HTTP half.

//!   caller's inbound headers never do. The caller's `Authorization: Bearer <paigasus-key>` must

//! - The upstream response is forwarded verbatim: a full body (non-stream) or an UNBUFFERED SSE
//!   stream. A non-2xx upstream (OpenAI's own error envelope) passes through unchanged.

# Task 14 report: the `/v1/responses` route

**Status: DONE_WITH_CONCERNS** (the concerns are below. None of them blocks the task.)

## Commits

- `6953d80b` refactor(rs): move the relay helpers out of the chat endpoint (SMA-769)
- `a5cfdf0d` feat(rs): serve /v1/responses with tool-call interception (SMA-769)

Both commits are signed. commitlint passed on both.

## What I implemented

- `dto::ResponsesRequest`. It has the fields of the brief. Every field is `Option`, so a JSON `null` reads as `None`. The other fields go to `extra` (flatten).
- `responses.rs`:
  - `RESPONSES_TERMINAL_SSE_ERROR`: the D13 literal of the Global Constraints, copied as written.
  - `RESPONSES: Endpoint`: `name: "responses"`, `UpstreamRoute::Responses`, `Format::OpenAiResponses`, the Task 13 readers (`responses_usage::non_stream_usage`, `StreamUsage::Responses(ResponsesUsageScanner::new())`), the D13 terminal frame, and `limits` = `ti.limits` with `max_record_bytes` and `max_held_bytes` from `state.responses`.
  - `create_response(State, Option<Extension<CallerContext>>, EnvelopeBytes)`. It is a copy of `chat_completions` that uses `RESPONSES`.
  - `parse_responses`. It reads the body into a `Value`. A syntax or EOF error gives `BadRequestBody`; a body that is not the request shape gives `InvalidRequestSchema`, as chat does (SMA-588). An `input` that is not a string or an array gives `InvalidRequestSchema`. Then it calls `refuse_stateful`. It computes the estimate with the Task 13 `request_tokens_estimate`, without changes. `model` is `"-"` when it is absent.
  - `refuse_stateful`. It refuses D4 (`background == Some(true)`) always. It refuses D3 only when interception is on. The order is `background`, `previous_response_id`, `conversation`, `prompt`, `input`, and the `param` is the field name.
- `mod.rs`: the route has its own router group. It is mounted only when `state.responses` is `Some`. The group has the `require_iam_auth` route layer (a second layer from the same `AuthState`) and `DefaultBodyLimit::max(settings.max_request_bytes)`. The chat router line is byte-identical.
- `ci/error-registry/check.py`: the `MANIFEST` row of the brief, as written.
- `tests/support/mod.rs`: the mock routes `POST /v1/responses` to the same `handle`. This is one line, and `cargo fmt` put it on one line.
- `paigasus-gateway-core/src/body.rs`: a new `BodyCalls::is_truncated()` accessor and its unit test (for C5, see below).

## How I met each carry and ruling

- **C1.** The move goes into a new `relay.rs` (`pub(crate) mod relay`): `StreamState`, `Relay`, `feed_scan`, `finish_scan` and `terminal_sse_error_stream`. It is in its own commit (`6953d80b`). It is a pure move: the code is byte-identical. Only the imports changed, and the two stale doc references of Task 10 M2 now point to `relay`/`pipeline::proxy`. `pipeline.rs` and `interception.rs` now import from `relay`. The chat unit tests stay in `chat.rs` and import `terminal_sse_error_stream` from `relay`. No test was moved or changed. SVC gave 379/379 after the move, the same list as before.
- **C2.** One shared switch. The pipeline already reads `state.capabilities.chat_stream` for every endpoint, so the Responses route obeys the same `stream_enabled`. That was the smaller change: no code change, no new key. `streaming_obeys_stream_enabled` proves it (400 `streaming-disabled`, `param: "stream"`, no upstream call, and the non-stream request still passes). The "chat completion …" log texts are not changed (they are for Task 15).
- **C3.** The intercepting relay calls `feed_scan` before `Interceptor::push`. `drain_for_billing` reads what is left after an early end. `a_terminal_event_over_1_mib_is_charged_with_interception_on_and_off` (1.5 MiB terminal, a held and rewritten stream with one blocked call) gives off `[4242]` and on `[4242]`. I split the over-16 MiB case into its own test, `a_terminal_event_over_the_record_limit_is_charged_and_fails_closed`, so that mutation (c) could show that it bites on its own. It uses a 17 MiB terminal, interception on and AllowAll. The results: off `[9001]`, on `[9001]`. For Review Focus 5 it asserts these client bytes: status 200, no `CANARY`, the `(malformed)` notice for both held calls, and a client body under 1 MiB (the over-limit record is not forwarded). That matches the core `oversized_terminal` edge row (the `(malformed)` path, not D13).
- **C4.** `BodyCalls::report` already calls `self.code(..)`, and `forced` wins there. `intercept_body` uses that report, so the header uses `body::forced`. No code change was necessary. `a_non_stream_blocked_call_is_rewritten_with_the_header` asserts it over HTTP: an `incomplete` call with the AllowAll decider gets the header entry `decision: block, code: truncated` and the `(truncated)` rewrite.
- **C5.** `intercept_body` now checks `calls.is_truncated()`. It counts `OnFailure("truncated")`, as the stream's `truncate_open` does. Under `on_failure = allow` it forwards the body unchanged with no header, as the stream's `PassThrough` verdict does for the whole hold (D10: one hold per response). Under `block` the flow does not change: the forced `Truncated` wins. Chat and Anthropic force nothing, so `is_truncated()` is always false there. Tests: the `allow` case and the `block` case are both in `a_non_stream_blocked_call_is_rewritten_with_the_header`, and the core unit test is `is_truncated_follows_the_forced_codes`. **Conflict that I resolved by the rulings:** the C5 text says "`block` answers 502 `tool-interception-malformed-response`" (it quotes the plan's Review Focus 3). Ruling F7 and the amended spec § 6.5 say that a not-completed client-run item under `block` is blocked `Truncated` and rewritten, not 502. The rules say that the rulings override plan text, so I followed F7: `block` gives the `(truncated)` rewrite. The 502 under `block` applies to a body that cannot be checked (`a_malformed_body_is_a_502_under_block`, a duplicate key). Under `allow` that body goes through unchanged.
- **C6.** HTTP level: `stateful_requests_are_refused_before_admission` sends six refused bodies (background, the three D3 fields, a typed and an untyped `item_reference`) with interception on. Each one gets 400, the code `responses-stateful-not-supported`, its `param`, the type `invalid_request_error` and the exact message. After those six, `store.checks() == 0` and the upstream count is 0. Then a body with `null` values and `background: false` gets 200 with a limit of one, and the next request gets 429. `background_is_refused_with_interception_off` shows that D4 holds and D3 passes with interception off. Unit level: `stateful_fields_are_refused_only_when_non_null` covers every field, on and off, the order, and a replayed `message`/`function_call` item with an `id` (that item passes).
- **C7.** `the_route_is_404_when_disabled` sends the request with and without a credential, and both get 404 (no credential challenge). It sends no upstream request, and chat still answers. The same test turns the route on and gets 200. Every other test in the file runs with the route on.
- **D5.** In `the_request_goes_to_the_responses_path` the body has odd whitespace, `"store":true`, an unknown key and `1.50`. The recorded upstream body is byte-equal to it, with interception off and on. The path is `/v1/responses`. The upstream gets the real key and no header holds the caller key.
- **F1.** I changed one existing test file: `tests/support/mod.rs` got one `.route("/v1/responses", post(handle))`. No existing assertion changed. The `nextest list` diff against the baseline shows additions only: 5 unit tests and 18 service tests.
- **F12.** See the mutation table.
- **Chat unchanged.** All 18 existing service test files pass unchanged.

## Tests and results (final run, after the last mutation restore)

- `SVC` (`cargo nextest run --locked -p paigasus-gateway`): 402 passed, 0 skipped (1 leaky: the reqwest-error unit test, the same as the chat test that it copies). The baseline was 379.
- `CORE` (`cargo nextest run --locked -p paigasus-gateway-core`): 315 passed, 1 skipped.
- `LINT` (`cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings && cargo fmt --check`): clean.
- `python3 -I ci/error-registry/check.py --self-test`: `self-test: OK`. `--single-site`: rc 0.
- No Docker-backed Redis test failed, so no re-run was necessary.

## TDD evidence

- RED (unit): I wrote `responses.rs` first with `refuse_stateful` as a stub that refuses nothing. `cargo nextest run --locked -p paigasus-gateway --lib responses:: dto::` gave `8 tests run: 7 passed, 1 failed`, and the failure was `stateful_fields_are_refused_only_when_non_null` (panic at responses.rs:186). The frame and input tests passed at once, because I wrote the constant and the input check before the run. They are not a RED proof. Their bite is shown by the registry gate and by the mutations.
- GREEN (unit): the same command after the implementation gave `8 tests run: 8 passed`.
- Service tests: I wrote them after I mounted the route, so I have no RED run of the whole file. The first run of the file gave 15/17. The two failures were in the test: the mock answered `{}`, which is correctly a 502 under interception. A second failure in the test came later, and it was real information: `the_body_limit_is_the_responses_limit` with a 4 MiB cap got 413 at exactly the cap. The cause is that the mock's own axum router keeps the 2 MiB default limit and the gateway forwards its 413. The test now uses the spec cap for the 2 MiB pass and a 1.5 MiB cap for the exact-cap and `cap + 1` rows. That cap is under axum's default, so the test fails when the route's layer is missing. The mutation battery below is the RED proof for the security core.

## Mutation battery (ruling F12): each mutation compiles

Command for each run: `cargo nextest run --locked -p paigasus-gateway --no-fail-fast -E '<filter>'`. To restore each mutation, I deleted the marked insert with Edit. I did not use `git checkout`. After the last restore, `grep -rn MUTATION rs/` finds nothing, and `git diff` shows no change in `pipeline.rs`.

| | Mutation | Result |
|---|---|---|
| (a) | `refuse_stateful`: `if !interception \|\| black_box(true)` (skip D3) | KILLED: `stateful_fields_are_refused_only_when_non_null` (unit), `stateful_requests_are_refused_before_admission` (HTTP) |
| (b) | `pipeline::proxy` stream arm: guard `if endpoint.name != "responses"` on the intercepting arm, `None` changed to `_` (a blocked streamed call is forwarded unchanged) | KILLED: `a_streamed_blocked_call_never_reaches_the_client`, `an_upstream_error_mid_hold_ends_with_the_d13_frame`, `a_stream_is_charged_its_usage`, `a_terminal_event_over_1_mib_is_charged_with_interception_on_and_off` |
| (c) | `interception::relay`: `feed_scan` behind `if black_box(false)` (no usage feed with interception on) | KILLED: `a_stream_is_charged_its_usage`, `a_terminal_event_over_1_mib_…`, `a_terminal_event_over_the_record_limit_is_charged_and_fails_closed`, and the existing `tool_interception::a_blocked_stream_charges_like_the_upstream` |
| (d) | `router`: the `DefaultBodyLimit` layer of the responses group removed | KILLED: `the_body_limit_is_the_responses_limit` (`left: 200, right: 413` at `cap + 1`) |
| (e, extra) | `intercept_body`: the C5 `allow` early return behind `&& black_box(false)` | KILLED: `a_non_stream_blocked_call_is_rewritten_with_the_header` |

After the last restore: SVC 402/402, CORE 315/315 (1 skipped), LINT clean.

## Files changed

- New: `rs/crates/services/paigasus-gateway/src/adapters/http/relay.rs` (commit 1)
- New: `rs/crates/services/paigasus-gateway/src/adapters/http/responses.rs`
- New: `rs/crates/services/paigasus-gateway/tests/responses_proxy.rs`
- Changed: `src/adapters/http/chat.rs`, `pipeline.rs` (imports and doc only, commit 1), `interception.rs`, `mod.rs`, `dto.rs`
- Changed: `tests/support/mod.rs` (one route)
- Changed: `rs/crates/libs/paigasus-gateway-core/src/body.rs` (`is_truncated` and its test)
- Changed: `ci/error-registry/check.py` (one `MANIFEST` row)

## Self-review

- The chat router line is byte-identical. The responses group builds its own auth layer, so no `auth.clone()` reflows the chat line.
- `responses_limits` falls back to `ti.limits` when `state.responses` is `None`. That case cannot occur, because the route is not mounted then. The fallback keeps the function total. It does not panic.
- `create_response` is `pub(crate)`, as `chat_completions` is. `RESPONSES` is `pub static`, as `CHAT` is (Task 10 M5 has the same note).
- The client-abort test does not use the abortable mock with interception on: the mock's frame `data: hold` is not Responses JSON. The plain-relay path is the one that G8 needs.

## Concerns

1. **`repo:http-extractor-envelope` is red before this task.** `python3 -I ci/http-extractor/check.py --check` fails on `pipeline.rs:73 fn proxy(…) takes Bytes`. I ran the gate on a `git archive` of `ec5e0031` (the commit before this task), and it fails there in the same way, so Task 10 started it. `proxy` is not a handler (its callers take `EnvelopeBytes`), so it needs a reasoned `ALLOW` row or a change of the gate's handler detection. I did not change the gate: that is outside the brief, and the decision is for the coordinator. My new handler `create_response` takes `EnvelopeBytes` and is not flagged.
2. **The `item_reference` rule is wider than the literal text.** In openai-python 3.48.0, `ItemReference` has `id` required and `type: Optional[Literal["item_reference"]]`. Thus `{"id":"msg_1"}` with no `type` is a reference to stored state. I refuse an input item whose `type` is `"item_reference"`, or whose `type` is absent or `null` and that has no `role`. The only other untyped item, the easy input message, always has `role`. This is stricter than the literal "type item_reference" (it fails closed), and the spec D3 intent requires it. Please confirm the rule, or record it in the spec.
3. **C5 versus F7** (see C5 above): under `block`, a truncated non-stream item gets the `(truncated)` rewrite (F7), not a 502.
4. **The mock keeps axum's 2 MiB body limit.** A service test cannot send more than 2 MiB through to the mock. I designed the body-limit test around this limit instead of a second edit to `tests/support/mod.rs`. If a later task needs larger upstream bodies, the mock needs `DefaultBodyLimit::disable()`.
5. The service tests have no RED run of their own (see TDD evidence). The mutations (a)–(e) are the evidence that they bite.

http-extractor-envelope:
    description: 'Assert no HTTP handler takes a bare `axum::Json` in request position, so a refused body cannot answer outside the IAM error envelope (SMA-587).'
    # WHY THIS EXISTS — a bare `axum::Json<T>` in REQUEST position answers a refused body
    # (malformed JSON, wrong content-type, schema mismatch, oversized body) with axum's default
    # PLAIN TEXT rejection, escaping the service's stable `{"error":{code,message}}` envelope.
    # SMA-587 converted fourteen handlers to the house `EnvelopeJson<T>`; nothing but this gate
    # stops a fifteenth being written with bare `Json<T>` tomorrow.
    #
    # WHY `inputs` IS THE ADAPTER TREE AND NOT A FILE LIST — like repo:error-code-single-site, this
    # gate's whole job is to notice a NEW handler in a NEW file. A narrow list would schedule it
    # only when an already-clean file changed, so the one case it exists for is the one case it
    # never runs on. The first glob is IDENTICAL to check.py's SCAN_GLOB on purpose: scheduling and
    # scanning must not be able to drift apart. Cheap for the same reason the other repo:* scans
    # are — a pure-python pass over 26 files, no cargo invocation (toolchain: 'system').
    #
    # `--self-test` runs FIRST and in the SAME script block, per repo:error-code-single-site: a
    # rotted checker must red rather than ship green, and the self-test's planted violations are
    # the only proof this gate can red at all (it carries no --negative-control mode).
    # `set -euo pipefail` is REQUIRED — Moon does not enable errexit for `script:` blocks, so
    # without it a failing --self-test would be masked by a passing --check.
    script: |
      set -euo pipefail
      python3 ci/http-extractor/check.py --self-test
      python3 ci/http-extractor/check.py --check
    toolchain: 'system'
    inputs:
      - 'rs/crates/services/*/src/adapters/http/**/*.rs'
      - 'ci/http-extractor/**/*'

message.content:
The coordinator sent a message while you were working:
Task 14 fix round 1. The review approved the task with Minor findings only. I raised one of them to Important under a coordinator ruling, and I send two more Minor fixes with it. Fix in new commits (do not amend). The full review is task-14-review.md in the SDD directory.

1. Important (raised by ruling): the D3 check depends on duplicate-key handling (responses.rs:88). serde_json keeps the last key, so `{"previous_response_id":"r","previous_response_id":null}` passes D3. If OpenAI keeps the first key, a stateful request bypasses interception (and the turn facts — tools, prior calls — could also differ from what the upstream reads). Ruling: with interception on, a /v1/responses request body that has a duplicate object key at ANY depth is refused with a 400 before admission (use the existing invalid-request error that chat uses for a body that parsed but did not match — `InvalidRequestSchema` or the closest existing code; do not add a new error code). Reuse the gateway-core strict parser (`paigasus-gateway-core/src/json.rs`, `parse_strict`) if it rejects duplicates and can be exposed cleanly; otherwise write a small duplicate-key check. With interception off, keep passing the body through (no refusal) — D3 does not apply then, but D4 `background` still does: make the D4 check also refuse a duplicate `background` key in both modes. Tests: a duplicate `previous_response_id` (non-null first, null last, and the reverse), a duplicate nested key inside an input item, a duplicate `background` with interception off; each refused before admission (uses no quota), and the same body without the duplicate passes.
2. Minor: `{"id":"msg_1","role":null}` passes the item_reference rule (responses.rs:139). Fail closed: an input item with no string `type` counts as an item_reference unless `role` is a string. Add the case.
3. Minor: no test pins `max_held_bytes` for the route (a compiled mutation that falls back to the shared limit survived all 18 responses_proxy tests; responses.rs:76). Add a test that kills that mutation (for example a non-stream body of about 5 MiB with one call, or whatever size sits between the shared limit and 32 MiB), and prove it by running that compiled mutation once, restored by deleting the insert.

Run the covering tests (the new unit tests in responses.rs, `cargo nextest run --locked -p paigasus-gateway --test responses_proxy`), then SVC and LINT, and `python3 ci/http-extractor/check.py --check`. Commit as `fix(rs): refuse duplicate keys in a responses request (SMA-769)` (and a second commit for 2+3 if you prefer), signed, your harness trailer. Append a fix section to task-14-report.md with the covering tests, the exact commands and output. Return the short contract. Same rules: Edit tool, one edit at a time; BLOCKED if the classifier refuses an edit; foreground only; no subagents.

Address this before completing your current task.
